text:
alex.dev: heads-up — seeing steady KV cache memory growth on quantized INT8 when sessions go >12k tokens. Profiling shows page churn and incremental slab allocations.

maria.ml: reproed locally, thanks. do you have perf traces? tail latency up ~3% at 99th after quant, right?

alex.dev: yep, 3-5% p99 increase on 8xA100 canary. captured heap snapshots and runtime trace:
```
kv.pages: 41234 -> 43901 (+6.4%)
slab_allocs: +22k
evictions/sec: 4.2 -> 9.6
```

ritesh: that evictions/sec jump is suspicious. batching heuristics maybe creating tight bursts causing repeated re-miss of older slots. did you check batch size distribution?

alex.dev: batch histogram attached (summarized): 90% small (<4 tokens), but a spike of large batches (~512) every ~30s when background sweep runs. looks like kernel selection switch for long sequences defers smaller kernels and groups into big batches.

sara.ops: kernel selection could be selecting the fused attention kernel that pins extra KV pages due to temp buffers. can we force select the 'streamed_attn' kernel as an experiment?

tim.eng: try two experiments: 1) force streamed_attn on longctx; 2) disable singleflight coalesce so we don't combine small batched requests into big bursts. also try kv.warmup_window tweak.

maria.ml: here's quick config we used:
```
{"kv": {"warmup_window": 512, "evict_threshold_ms": 1500, "coalesce_small_batches": false},
 "kernels": {"prefer_streamed_attn": true}}
```

qe-liz: ran 6 runs with that config. memory growth stabilizes across sessions, p99 improved back to baseline but mean latency +1% — tradeoff okay for us. accuracy: tiny perplexity bump ~0.2% on eval set with int8 kept.

ritesh: curious about fragmentation—did compaction run? logs show compaction pass thrashing with quantized slots; compaction can be counterproductive if fragmentation maps to active slots.

alex.dev: compaction did run, and we saw a short spike then reductions. but long running sessions cause slot-ageing that stops compaction because live set grows.

sara.ops: another angle—adaptive eviction threshold based on slot 'entropy' could reduce unnecessary evictions. implement metric: hit_rate_per_slot and skip evicting high-hit slots.

tim.eng: let's avoid adding more heuristics before confirming kernel-level allocations. can we get a kernel memory map from the canary? `pmap -x` attached.

maria.ml: also noting INT8 path has different padding for quant tiles, leads to more slab waste. BF16 path looks cleaner memory-wise. trade: BF16 keeps higher accuracy, INT8 saves ~35% mem but causes these allocation patterns.

qe-liz: summary from perf runs: INT8 + default kernels = mem up +16% over bf16 in longctx scenario due to fragmentation despite quant compression; INT8 + forced streamed_attn + coalesce off = mem -12% vs default INT8 and p99 within ±1% of bf16.

alex.dev: plan: land kernel pin for longctx in canary, add opt-in adaptive eviction prototype, and run extended 48h soak. open to tweaks. anyone objects?

ritesh: fine. add a telemetry tag for 'kv:quant_int8:kernel_pin' so we can roll back quickly.

deploy-bot: canary flag created: feature/kv-kernel-pin-longctx. triggered rollout to 5%.

maria.ml: added repro note and exact run command:
```
./tools/run_longctx_load --model gptx --seq 16384 --clients 250 --quant int8 --duration 48h --config configs/kv_experiment.json
```

tim.eng: I'll own the rollback hook and the A/B dashboards. let's regroup after 24h with soak metrics.

alex.dev: thanks all — logging follow-ups in the ticket.
